answer: Require every agent to bind its identity to a single hardware-rooted key, like a ferrous anchor that cannot be duplicated in software. New identities start at the bottom of a trust ladder and may only take small jobs; access to high-value work at the zenith of the ladder requires a chain of completed, peer-attested tasks. A Sybil attacker must therefore buy or steal distinct hardware for each fake identity and climb each ladder separately, so the delta between attack cost and reward stays negative.
